recommendedModel: Collection Multiplier (Mike's lean) — SHIP OPTION B FROM DAY ONE. power = START_ATTACK(6) × CLAWS_MULT(2.0)^clawsLevel × (1 + ΣformBonus[owned] + formBonus[active]). The active form's own bonus is double-counted, so switching to a higher form is a FELT damage jump, while owning ANY form is permanently net-positive. Full 20/20 collection = ×64 base (sum-to-63), plus the active double-count adds up to ×1.156. This is the Collection Multiplier model with its #1 killer risk (inert switching) pre-fixed by grafting the runner-up's felt-on-switch property.
why: Three lenses, one verdict. ECONOMY-INTEGRITY (the hardest gate, and the campaign's whole identity is the bounded 1e9 cap + earned statue finale): the Collection Multiplier scored 9/10 because (1+Σbonus) appears identically in attackPower (economy.js:107-111) AND clawsCost (economy.js:181-185), so it CANCELS in the cost:income ratio — verified the bounded invariant ratio stays exactly 2.000 at every multiplier and level. No other model preserves the gz-v16 cost==power==HP invariant for free; the Hybrid (also 9) requires you to manually thread collMult through clawsCost or it silently breaks, and FSCM (8) deliberately SOFTENS the invariant ~50×. LONG-TERM (World 2 / NG+): the additive (1+Σbonus) substrate is the cleanest prestige graft — a prestige factor or collection-memory is a one-line change, and the cancellation means stacked multiplier layers stay balanced automatically. PLAYER-EXPERIENCE: pure Option A scored 8 but its one hole — switching becomes weightless — is exactly the prompt's stated goal ('becoming Ghidorah/Mecha is FELT'). That hole is closed by Option B (verified cap-safe: claws-to-cap stays 22 at full collection). The two models that score higher on felt-switching (the Rank ladder, 7 PX) only do so by flattening every form to an identical ×2 AND collapsing form costs ~26× (super_mecha 90M→9.44M), which trivializes the very collection meant to motivate and forces a save-reshape. The re-priced base-jump (5 PX) and FSCM (deletes the becoming-the-monster beat) both fail the felt-fantasy bar. Collection Multiplier + Option B is the only model that wins economy-integrity AND long-term AND keeps the felt switch — with the smallest, formula-only migration. I verified against live code: economy.js:107-111 (attackPower), :181-185 (clawsCost), :194 (canFinale), :254 (buyClaws cap-deny), :24 (CAP_HP=max(ROW_HP)=1e9), :395/:401/:431 (save v:3 / load rejects v!==3 / clawsLevel clamp 0..64), and config.js:106-259 (the 20 forms, tier 0..19 monotonic global). playerExperienceNarrative:
FIRST FORM (the trap, killed): today buying burning (150) at L0 buys the SAME power as 84 coins of claws — a value-inversion that makes your first 'become a new monster' moment feel like a rip-off. Under this model, buying burning instantly multiplies power ×1.25 (6 → 7.5) the moment you own it, on ANY active form, AND if you switch to it the active double-count makes it hit even harder. The aspirational beat finally points the right way: a new monster is always strictly new progress.

MID-GAME (the collection becomes a power meter): every form you buy lifts EVERY owned form's contribution, so X/20 is a literal, legible power bar (full = ×64). Recruiting the Ghidorah family (+10 to the sum) is a felt run of upgrades; completing Mecha (+26) is the biggest jump in the game. You never face a 'why buy this, I've out-leveled it' dead form — the additive sum means a cheap early form still pays forever.

THE SWITCH (Option B — the prompt's stated goal, delivered): switching active form is NOT weightless. Wielding super_mecha when you own it adds its +10 bonus a second time — the dream monster IS your hardest hitter, live, on screen, the same second you press Switch. You can still switch to a favorite kaiju's ATTACK STYLE (beam / DoT cloud / 3-bolt / dive AoE / volley) and the worst-case damage delta is tiny (you never trade away your whole build), so picking the monster you love to BE costs almost nothing — but picking the strongest costs a real, felt step up.

FINALE (the climax intact): the bounded climb survives untouched. Full collection gives a 6-claws head-start (22 vs 28 steps to 1e9), so the X/20 chase is rewarded with a faster, EARNED victory lap — but you still must grind the deep-tier income wall (the 90M top forms) and buy 22 claws to one-shot the statue. The 'MAXIMUM POWER — find and smash the Statue' beat fires exactly as designed. Collection accelerates the win; it never shortcuts the wall.

risks: INERT SWITCHING if Option B is NOT shipped: pure Option A makes the active form contribute zero live damage, relocating the most tactile beat in a tap-to-smash game off the switch. MITIGATION: ship Option B from day one (verified cap-safe, claws-to-cap stays 22). This is the single most important call — do not ship A-only.

MIGRATION PERCEPTION: a deep v3 save's displayed power number visibly changes on load (active-base no longer multiplies). Without the one-time 'progress intact' toast, players read it as a nerf. The toast is mandatory, not polish.

TABLE-SUM DRIFT: the clean ×64 target depends on ΣformBonus===63. A future World-2 form added without re-balancing breaks the legible 2^N rebate (cosmetic, cap still holds). The boot-time assert makes drift LOUD, not silent — but it's a permanent ~20-number hand-tune per World (the maintainability tax this model trades for per-unlock feel control).

INVISIBLE VALUE: the always-worth-it property is real but unfelt unless the shop copy + HUD X/20 meter ship. The UI rewording (economy.js:679/748/764) is load-bearing — skip it and you re-create the 'why buy this form?' confusion the rework exists to kill.

EARLY-FORM EFFICIENCY: the +25–60% relative jumps on cheap forms slightly over-reward rushing the cheapest forms. Bounded to a 6-step total rebate so the blast radius is contained; if playtest shows a degenerate 'buy all cheap forms to skip a claws step', flatten the wyrm band (0.25→0.2 etc.).

STALE MEMO: collectionMult must be recomputed on EVERY ownedFormIds OR activeFormId change (buyForm, switchForm, load). A stale cache silently mis-scales all damage AND the cap gate. Recompute in afterPurchase/switchForm/load; never persist it.

runnerUpAndWhatToGraft: RUNNER-UP: the Active-form ×2 Rank Ladder (power = 6 × 2^(rank+claws)). It is the best-scaling formula on the table (single closed form, World-N = append ranks, NG+ = a rank offset that drops into the exponent) and it owns the felt-switch beat natively (each form IS a permanent ×2 you feel on switch). I did NOT pick it because (a) its suggested 3× repricing collapses form costs ~26× (super_mecha 90M→9.44M), trivializing the collection the rework is meant to motivate, and the economy-integrity lens scored it only 6 for exactly this mid-game pacing collapse; (b) the uniform ×2 ladder flattens every form to numerically identical, so collection reads as a flat checklist; (c) it forces a real save-reshape (the log2 clawsLevel bridge) vs the Collection Multiplier's formula-only migration. WHAT TO GRAFT: I already grafted its single best property — felt-on-switch — into the winner via Option B (active double-count), which buys the 'I AM the dream monster and I hit harder' beat WITHOUT the cost-trivialization or save-reshape. ALSO WORTH GRAFTING for World 2: the rank-ladder reviewer's correct observation that the live `tier` field (config.js, 0..19 monotonic global) already IS a clean global rank — if Mike ever wants a SECOND felt axis later, formMult(tier)=small-curve is a zero-new-field add that composes cleanly with the collection multiplier. FROM FSCM, graft the named-set-milestone UI framing ('Complete the Ghidorahs — ×N') as a presentation layer over the additive sum: it makes the 5 families feel like chunky goals without changing the (always-positive, cap-safe) additive math.
